text:
Leaf by leaf the tender spring

restores the greenness of the fields,

and, freed from the ice, the brook flees,

mocking the meadow.


Awakened yesterday to the first song,

the wild sparrow senses its wing,

and through the light that spills and flows

climbs and descends the birdlike scale.


Now the poppy sheds its glow,

and the dandelion its golden plume;

everything throws itself into the feast of color;


only in the clear blue, blurred by nothing,

a torn and slack cloud floats,

like a briefest enclosure of foam.

translation.title: Leaf by Leaf the Tender Spring...
translation.editorial_note: The translation keeps the spring sonnet's restored green, bird-scale, color feast, and solitary cloud.
